# 佛說佛地經

**ID:** T0680
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 唐 玄奘譯
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 645
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0680

## Contributors
- 玄奘 (A000294)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T680 in one fascicle is [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s translation of the *Buddhabhūmi-sūtra*, the principal Mahāyāna scriptural source for the doctrine of the five types of buddha-knowledge or *jñāna* (五種菩提): mirror-like (大圓鏡智), equality (平等性智), discernment (妙觀察智), accomplishing-action (成所作智), and the all-pervading dharmadhātu wisdom (法界體性智 / 清淨法界). Translated at Hóngfúsì 弘福寺 in Cháng'ān in **Zhēnguān 19 (645 CE)**, the year of [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s return from India — the colophon "大唐三藏法師玄奘奉詔譯" is preserved at the head of the witness, which opens with the same rich seven-jewel-Buddhaland *nidāna* setting that [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s *[Jiě shēnmì jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353)* employs.

**Abstract**

The *Buddhabhūmi-sūtra* (Tib. *Sangs rgyas kyi sa'i mdo*) is one of the small group of Yogācāra-related sūtras that [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) translated immediately upon his return to China in 645. It serves as the scriptural ground for the *Buddhabhūmi-vyākhyāna* (*Fódìjīng lùn* 佛地經論), the major Yogācāra commentary by Bandhuprabha 親光 et al., which [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) also translated as [T1530](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0151) in 649–650. Together with the *Saṃdhinirmocana* ([KR6i0353](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353)), the *Mahāyāna-saṃgraha* (《攝大乘論》, T1594), and the *Yogācāra-bhūmi* (《瑜伽師地論》, T1579), the *Buddhabhūmi-sūtra* defined the doctrinal core of the Cí'ēn / Fǎxiàng school of Tang Yogācāra.

The Sanskrit original is lost; the sūtra is preserved only in Chinese (T680) and Tibetan (D 275). The doctrine of the five buddha-knowledges that the sūtra systematizes — and the four-knowledge schema (四智) which is its more familiar later derivative, omitting *dharmadhātu*-essence-knowledge — became foundational for East-Asian Mahāyāna in general and for tantric Buddhism's mapping of the five buddhas (五方佛) onto the five wisdoms in particular. The text is brief and dense, depicting the buddhaland *Vijñapti* with elaborate visual detail before unfolding the doctrine of the five wisdoms in dialogue with the bodhisattva *Miàoshēngshēng* 妙生 (*Suviśiṣṭa*-mati).

Related canonical texts: commentary on this sūtra: *[Fódì jīng lùn 佛地經論](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0151)* (T1530, by Bandhuprabha et al., trans. Xuánzàng).
